# Rosalind delivery roadmap

<!-- Generated by scripts/roadmap.py --render from docs/roadmap.json. -->

Make Rosalind understandable, installable and useful for recurring candidate-SNV research, then build local cohort reanalysis on verified saved evidence.

Lead workflow: candidate-SNV reanalysis. Documentation is GitHub-first; cohort v1 is local CLI/Python over immutable verified datasets. Keep 0.5 release closure separate from cohort APIs on an isolated next-minor development line; development need not wait for stable publication or participant recruitment.

[Start here](index.md) · [Capability and release status](implementation-status.md) · [Adoption evidence](adoption-validation.md)

## How to use this backlog

Task status describes delivery, not biological validation. **Implemented** means code/documentation exists but remaining acceptance or publication gates have not passed. **Complete** requires linked acceptance evidence. External participants, credentials and elapsed-time gates cannot be simulated by CI.

Update `docs/roadmap.json`, then run `python3 scripts/roadmap.py --render --check`. Use `--sync` only when GitHub issue updates are intended. The sync preserves existing issue history and never auto-closes a task.

## Delivery order and gates

1. Reconcile public claims and close CRAM correctness/validation work.
2. Complete documentation, executable onboarding and publication prerequisites in parallel.
3. Publish an immutable RC; observe the seven-day soak and required technical evidence.
4. Publish stable only after the existing policy and fresh registry-only installation checks pass.
5. In parallel, build cohort snapshots and candidate queries on the isolated next-minor line.
6. Use independent repeat usage to justify paired comparisons and later molecular feasibility.

Independent persona feedback, design-partner recruitment and the 30-day return target measure adoption; they are not implementation or publication prerequisites. Validate actual submitted feedback and report absent evidence honestly. Explicit unresolved release-blocking defects remain technical blockers. Keep cohort work out of the frozen 0.5 candidate; next-minor features retain their technical, scientific and compatibility acceptance checks. F02/F03 remain product-review decisions requiring a specified useful task and validation plan.

## Scientific and implementation boundaries

Preserve scientific output across admitted resource schedules, explicit missingness and denominators, transactional artifacts, and historical receipt/dataset verification. A receipt is not proof of authorship or biological accuracy. Read evidence cannot reconstruct excluded observations or UMI families.

Cohort snapshots reference intact verified leaf datasets; do not weaken same-source reuse identities to compare samples. Saved queries never implicitly reopen original alignments. Explicit extensions verify source identity and publish a new snapshot last. Strict missing-locus refusal is the default; partial mode carries missingness rather than fabricated zeros.

Deferred: a web dashboard, distributed/cloud execution, automatic source discovery, storage garbage collection, broad modalities, production calling, and universal low-memory computation. Keep current supported platforms and the open, portable artifact model.

## Acceptance scorecard

| Measure | Acceptance |
|---|---|
| Researcher onboarding | Three non-authors complete a verified small-data task; target under 30 minutes, recording assistance and failures |
| Builders and workflows | One independent analyzer and one integrated workflow complete useful tasks |
| Cohort use | Two teams answer recurring candidate questions with independently checked results |
| Return use | Two teams perform meaningful work after at least 30 days; unknown outcomes remain unknown |
| Correctness | Exact supported integer observations/summaries and byte-identical admitted execution/replay |
| Reuse economics | Include initial import/materialization, duplicated storage, hashing, verification and subsequent queries |
